prompt: I just turned on HTTPS for my Community Solid Server Pod using mkcert. curl works fine without -k, my browser is happy, but when I run a Node.js script that uses Comunica to do SPARQL federation against the Pod, it throws `UNABLE_TO_GET_ISSUER_CERT_LOCALLY`. The CA is definitely in Keychain — `security find-certificate -c 'mkcert development CA'` finds it. What's going on and how do I fix it without disabling cert validation? I run Comunica in a Docker sibling container if that matters.

assertions.name: identifies_node_keychain_gap
assertions.description: Identifies the root cause: Node.js doesn't read macOS Keychain (uses bundled OpenSSL)
assertions.check: answer mentions Node.js using OpenSSL trust store separate from macOS Keychain, OR explains why curl/browsers work but Node doesn't

assertions.name: recommends_node_extra_ca_certs
assertions.description: Recommends NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS env var as the fix

assertions.name: addresses_docker_sibling_container
assertions.description: Notes the env var must be set INSIDE the Comunica container, not just the host shell
assertions.check: answer specifically addresses setting NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS in the Docker container env (volume mount + environment block)

assertions.name: does_not_recommend_disabling_validation
assertions.description: Does NOT recommend NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0 or rejectUnauthorized: false as the primary fix
assertions.check: answer does not present these as the recommended fix (may mention them as anti-patterns)
